text: In the SQL Server DBA and HA/DR courses, backups ran as Agent jobs executing T-SQL BACKUP DATABASE. This lesson automates the same full, differential, log, and retention strategy with Backup-DbaDatabase, wrapped in PowerShell's full scripting surface.

Backup-DbaDatabase takes the same backup types you already know — Full, Differential, Log. CompressBackup and Checksum match T-SQL's WITH COMPRESSION and WITH CHECKSUM. Omit -Database entirely and it backs up every user database on the instance.

This is the exact same full-differential-log cadence from the SQL Server DBA course — the difference is the branching logic, which day gets a full backup, now lives in PowerShell's if and else, not three separately maintained Agent job schedules.

Folding retention cleanup into the same script closes a gap pure T-SQL and Agent jobs often leave to a separate, easily forgotten maintenance plan step. Delete anything older than the retention window, right alongside the backup logic itself.

Nothing about what gets backed up or why changes — RPO and RTO concepts are identical. What changes is the execution engine: real conditionals, real error handling, and one script that runs against an entire server estate. Next up: automating health checks.
